newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar up ahead of Moslem feast, low arrivals.
newsitem.headline: India sugar up ahead of Moslem feast, low arrivals.

text.p: Sugar prices extended gains as high consumer demand and restricted arrivals kept prices high ahead of a Moslem festival, dealers said on Friday.
Fears of lower sugar production in the current year kept the undercurrent firm.
Traders expected sugar production of 15/20 million tonnes for the 1996/97 sugar year against 16.40 million tonnes in 1995/96. The sugar year begins from October in India.
In ready delivery sugar S-30 moved up by 10 rupees to 1,245/1,285 rupees per quintal, while M-30 rose by 6 rupees to 1,300/1,371 rupees per quintal.
Sugar mill delivery remained steady at 1,190/1,200 rupees per quintal amid lower outstation enquiries.
